name: std_ConstructArray
signature: void *std_ConstructArray(void *base, void (*ctor)(void *), u32 elemSize, u32 count)
summary: Runs a constructor callback once per element of a raw array, advancing by elemSize and stopping after count elements; returns the array base, never the callback result. This is the helper every array-of-objects constructor in the binary was compiled down to.
evidence: Body: iVar1 = base; while (arg4) { (*arg2)(iVar1); iVar1 += arg3; } return base. Disassembly shows an actual `blx r6` per element, so the second argument is a code pointer, not a fill value. 593 callers including Engine_Initialize@0x101b74, 0x109990 (2 slots of 10 bytes at +0x31ce), 0x1064d8 (5 slots of 0x10 at +0x34), 0x1064d8/0x15cdc4. Every code-pointer argument used with it dereferences to a code address in code.decompressed.bin: g_0010672c -> 0x107f6c, g_00109d94 -> 0x10f3b4, g_0010e42c/30/34 -> 0x116798/0x1167b0/0x116780, g_00114270 -> 0x11982c, g_001144b0 -> 0x119838, g_0011deac -> 0x1235e0, g_00124478 -> 0x1150a0, g_001221bc -> 0x106a10; and the object each ctor fills starts with a vtable pointer (e.g. g_00106728 -> 0x7821c8). This is the array-of-objects construction helper, not memset/memcpy (N_081's merge note guesses memcpy for this address - that is wrong).

name: maybe_std_StrtodThunk
summary: Eight-byte pass-through trampoline that branches straight into std_strtod with the caller's registers untouched, so it is an alternate entry to the double parser rather than atof (atof would clear the endptr argument).
evidence: Bytes at 0x1005ee: 10 b5 00 f0 4a fc 10 bd = push {r4,lr}; bl 0x100e88 (std_strtod); pop {r4,pc}; no argument setup at all. Only callers are 0x502e20 and 0x503298, i.e. the 0x50xxxx math/format block, not the libc printf core.

name: std_mbstowcs
signature: int std_mbstowcs(u16 *dst, const u8 *src, u32 maxChars, mbstate *state)
summary: Converts a multibyte byte string (current locale encoding) into a 16-bit wide-character buffer, one character per call to the locale decoder, stopping at the terminating NUL or after maxChars characters, and returns the number of wide characters stored.
evidence: Loop reads one byte, calls 0x2ff9d0 (locale mbrtowc dispatch: it tail-calls the encoding function at state->f_103) and stores the resulting wchar with `*(short*)(arg1 + i*2)`; loop exits on wchar==0 or i>=arg3; callers 0x502650/0x502928 are in the libc string/format block next to std_mbrlen@0x100658 and std_mbrtowc@0x10067c.

name: std_wcsncpy
summary: Copies at most count wide characters and zero-fills the remainder: once the source NUL is copied the source pointer stops advancing, which is exactly the wcsncpy contract.
evidence: Body: while (count--) { *dst++ = *src; if (*src) src++; } return dst; the conditional advance is the c89 wcsncpy padding idiom. 16 callers include Actor_CompareNames@0x147dc4, Text_LayoutPage_BuildLines@0x2fd45c and 0x1918 0x19180c (seven-character short-name field of a text page).

name: Snd_StreamSlot_UpdateAll
summary: Per-frame update of the six banks of streamed-audio slots (6 x 0x20 slots of 0x24 bytes at +0x110). For every slot whose state bits are set it validates the slot's pack handle, completes or cancels the pending async transfer, releases the pack record and adjusts the busy counters.
evidence: Slot records are 0x24 bytes at self+0x110 (index = bank*0x20 + slot, six banks, f_d4/f_d8/f_dc are the busy counts, f_f8/f_e0 the per-bank bitmasks); state word at +4 with bits 2/4; pack handle at +5 is validated against g_00105aec/g_00105af0 exactly like Pack_FreeHandleEntry@0x1241d0; transfers go through 0x10df00 and complete via 0x10ef64/0x10efb8; gain changes via Snd_FadeChannelToGain@0x114cfc. Callers 0x10293c (frame tasks), 0x1ecd08, 0x1ecd6c, 0x1edab4 (sound).

name: maybe_Snd_StreamVoice_UpdateAlt
summary: Same streamed-voice state machine as 0x105afc. Ghidra decoded the tail bytes of the neighbouring ARM routine as a separate Thumb function, so this entry is a mis-split duplicate of the stop/fade/ring-advance code.
evidence: 0x105ace is exactly the end of 0x105584 and sits in ARM code (the ARM twin 0x105afc is 0x2e bytes later), yet the batch marks it thumb; the pseudo-C is structurally identical to 0x105afc (same 0x40-entry rings f_a48/f_a4c, state byte f_a50, same callees 0x116e44 / 0x114cfc / 0x10df00).

name: Snd_StreamVoice_Update
summary: Drives one streamed-audio voice for a frame: consumes the 64-entry command ring at +0x1848 (start / set-buffer / stop / fade / delay), submits pack-streamed chunks into the voice's two buffers, advances the fade timer at +0x1a54 and runs the nine-state machine at +0x1a50.
evidence: Called by Snd_RequestBgmPlay@0x1ec1d0 and Snd_RequestBgmStop@0x1ee4f8 plus 0x10293c; ring of 0x40 records of 8 bytes at +0x1848 read via f_1a48/f_1a4c, states 0..8 in f_1a50, fade compares f_1a54 with f_1a58, calls 0x10df00 (async read into a buffer), Snd_FadeChannelToGain@0x114cfc, 0x116e44 (per-voice parameter), and the pack free path 0x1241d0.

name: maybe_Os_OwnerTable_Init
summary: Initialises a small owner/handle table: stores the vtable word, walks a chain of 0x30-byte sub-blocks starting at +4 and default-constructs five 0x10-byte records at +0x34.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2, then a repeated 0x109558(arg+1) / 0x109558(&x->f_30) chain (Ghidra lost the individual calls), closing with func_00100050(&x->f_34, g_0010672c, 0x10, 5). No callers; the neighbours are Gfx_ReleaseFinishedUploads@0x106280, Os_SetRuntimeFlag@0x106440 and Os_GetThreadClass@0x106460.

name: maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine
signature: void maybe_Snd_ShutdownEngine(SndEngine *engine, u32 arg2, u32 *mask, int count)
summary: Closes the engine's session handles and tears down active voices: for every set bit of the caller's id mask it releases the 0x1c-byte voice records (honouring the 0x8000 flag table at g_00109894) and finally signals the waiting lock.
evidence: svc 0x24 (wait) plus svc 0x23 (CloseHandle) on ->f_344, sets state bytes f_358/f_348, calls 0x10ea00 (buffer release) on +0x340; then loops `mask = *(u32*)(arg3 + i*4)` bit by bit over 0x1c-byte records at self->f_24 + i*0x1c calling 0x10df40 / 0x10df90 / 0x10e174; asserts through 0x118100 when *g_0010988c < 0. Ghidra dropped several registers (unaff_r5/r6), so the object identity comes from the callees.

name: maybe_Gfx_Context_ResetState
summary: Constructor/reset of the display context: stores the vtable, clears the counters at +0x294c..+0x2988 and the table at +0xc738, then default-constructs two 10-byte entries there.
evidence: *arg1 = arg2; explicit zero stores to arg1[0xa53..0xa62], arg1[0xa99..0xa9b], arg1[0xb48..0xb4a]; ends with func_00100050((int)arg1 + 0x31ce, g_00109d94, 10, 2). Neighbours Gfx_CopyFramebuffer@0x10ad60, Gfx_SwapFrameBuffers@0x109e28, Gfx_ReleaseBufferRecord@0x109e88.

name: Pack_HandleTable_Get
summary: Lazily creates and returns the global pack-handle table: allocates a zeroed singleton, constructs its twenty 0x28-byte handle entries at +0x18 and caches the pointer.
evidence: One-shot flag g_0010b040, cache g_0010b044, size g_0010b04c aligned to 0x10 through 0x11cfac, std_bzero + 0x1242ac (the 0x14-entry pack handle ctor at g_00124478), then ->f_4 = g_0010b050 + 0x18. Callers Fs_CacheSet_Initialize@0x103724, Gfx_SubmitDrawList@0x10411c, Fs_NamedObject_LoadSimple@0x3882f0, Ui_Window_SetColorByState@0x38859c.

name: maybe_Svc_RequestWithSetup
signature: int maybe_Svc_RequestWithSetup(u32 cmd, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Wraps a service request in the engine's global lock: queries the session state, waits (sleeping) while the peer reports busy, sends the caller's three-word request and restores the lock.
evidence: 0x119ba8/0x119e1c bracket every step (global lock), 0x114514(0xffffffff,&a,&b,&c) plus 0x11a36c polling with 0x11cc94 sleeps, then 0x1144c0(cmd,arg2,arg3) issues the real svc 0x32 request; errors go to 0x118924(result, 0x10ce1c / 0x10ce58 / 0x10cef8). Callers are the two sound-state updaters 0x1078a8 and 0x1079c0.

name: maybe_Svc_RequestWithRetry
signature: int maybe_Svc_RequestWithRetry(u32 req, u32 a2, u32 a3, u32 a4)
summary: Same locked session wrapper, but it retries the request while the service returns one of three 'try again' codes, sleeping ten time units between attempts, and reports a negative result through the error handler.
evidence: Loop calls 0x1145c4(arg1..arg4) and repeats while the result equals g_0010d640 / g_0010d644 / g_0010d648, sleeping via 0x11cc94(g_0010d64c * 10); arms/clears the in-call flag with 0x11391c / 0x113980, error path 0x11ed40(result, 0x10d5d4); caller maybe_Snd_UpdateStateB@0x1079c0.

name: Container_ForEachPair
summary: Iterates a key/value container and dispatches every entry to the owner object's vtable slot +0xc; returns 0 as soon as an entry cannot be read and 1 after the whole map was walked.
evidence: 0x114dd0 builds the iterator (element count = *iterator), the loop calls 0x115d78(it,&key,&value) and then `(**(code **)(*arg1 + 0xc))(arg1,key,value)`; bail-out returns the partially read value when 0x115d78 fails.

name: Snd_QueueWaveCommand
signature: void Snd_QueueWaveCommand(u32 unused, u32 waveAddress, u32 waveLength)
summary: Queues a 'set wave data' command on the sound engine: allocates a six-word command node, tags it 0x31, stores the caller's buffer address and length, links it into the submit chain and flushes the queue.
evidence: Engine singleton 0x11b7e8; node alloc 0x11b57c(engine,6); node byte +4 = 0x31; f_10/f_14 = arg2/arg3; submit 0x11b89c; then 0x114e60(engine,1) and 0x115018 wait for the command id. Only caller is 0x105584 (streamed-voice update), which passes the voice buffer pointer and its size.

name: Snd_ReleaseAllChannels
summary: Destroys every channel object of the engine (0x18 records of 0x5c bytes), rebuilds the three 128-entry parameter tables and drains the pending command queue before the engine stops.
evidence: Loop i < self->f_18 calling 0x11ae88(self->f_1c + i*0x5c) = per-channel release; then three func_00100050(stack, g_0010e42c/0x10e430/0x10e434, 0xc, 0x80) = construct 3 x 128 twelve-byte records (128 = the mixer's voice count); finally 0x11b7e8 (engine), 0x114fac (queue drain) and 0x114e60(engine,0). Callers 0x108f32 (engine shutdown) and 0x10967c.

name: maybe_Snd_SetVoiceLoop
signature: void maybe_Snd_SetVoiceLoop(SndVoice *voice, int restart, u32 rate, float startPos)
summary: Programs a voice's sample-loop window: converts the caller's rate and start position into a loop length (clamped to at least one sample), stores start/length/end and switches the voice into the 'loop prepared' state; with restart == 0 the existing loop is first torn down.
evidence: Reads state byte f_a1 (0..3), locks the 4-word loop record with 0x11cbd4(&voice->f_78), computes (int)((g_0010e53c - s0) * (float)rate) with a minimum of 1, writes f_78/f_7c/f_80/f_84 and sets f_a1 = 3 (restart) or 1 plus flag f_a3. Used by 0x105584, 0x105ace, 0x105afc and 0x1eb8c8 - all streamed-voice code; the float argument arrives in s0, which is why Ghidra's signature only shows three parameters.

name: maybe_Ui_PartyStatus_InitMemberData
summary: Initialises the member/parameter region of the party-status window: fills the 31-byte flag array with 0xff, zeroes the 0x36 per-member records and resets the 90-entry name table plus the 0x168 / 0x64 / 0x54 sub-tables to their defaults.
evidence: Called with the window pointer from 0x19371c; uses std_bzero@0x116ae0, std_memcpy@0x116c10 and the fill helpers 0x111384 / 0x1113ec; every offset it touches (0x2780, 0x2964, 0x2a70, 0x31ce, 0x4b30, 0x5418, 0x5762, 0x59ac, 0x89a8) lies inside the >0x974c-byte object built by 0x19371c / 0x1939c0.

name: maybe_Gfx_InitRegisterTables
signature: void maybe_Gfx_InitRegisterTables(GfxState *state, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Builds the GPU's static state tables: copies the register table, expands four 0xbd-terminated id lists into bitsets, and fills the per-format value/valid arrays with the constants 0x800, 0x3f000, 0x3c00, 1 and 0.
evidence: Only caller is Gfx_InitializeContext@0x109fb0. Writes state->f_13a4..f_176c (a value array plus the parallel valid-byte array at +0x16b1), has a switch over indices 0x61..0xb3 selecting 0x3c00 / 0x3f000 / 0x800 / 1 / 0, and ends with the `while (i != 0xbd) { bits[i>>5] |= 1 << (i & 31); }` idiom (0xbd is the list terminator).

name: std_VectorInsertU32
summary: std::vector<u32>::insert: with spare capacity it shifts the tail right with memmove and stores the new word; otherwise it doubles the capacity and copies both halves into a fresh block.
evidence: Disassembly 0x11108c: ldrd r0,r1,[r6,#4] (begin/end), compares end to capacity, `addhi r7,r2,#4` when pos == end, three calls to 0x111378 with (dst,src,bytes) move the two halves, and the new capacity is `size ? size*2 : 1` (lslne r8,r0,#1 / moveq r8,#1).

name: std_VectorInsertU32Copy
summary: A second, instruction-identical instantiation of std::vector<u32>::insert; two translation units emitted their own copy, so the game contains both.
evidence: Disassembly 0x11117c..0x111268 is instruction-for-instruction identical to 0x11108c..0x111174 apart from the branch offsets; both call 0x111378 (memmove) three times with the same register setup.

name: std_memmove
summary: memmove: copies bytes in whichever direction is safe (backwards when the regions overlap and dst > src) using 4-byte words with a byte tail, and returns dst.
evidence: 0x111378 jumps into 0x1112ec, which starts `subs r3,r0,r1; cmphs r2,r3; bls 0x116a14` (no overlap -> forward memcpy) and otherwise copies backwards with `ldr/str [r0,#-4]!`; 63 callers, all vector/array moves (e.g. 0x18c544, 0x194408, 0x194220).

name: maybe_Buffer_ResetDoubleBuffer
summary: Zeroes both 0x84-byte halves of a double-buffered record and marks the two slots empty (-1), i.e. the reset half of a double-buffered object cache.
evidence: std_bzero(self,0x84); std_bzero(&self->f_84,0x84); f_108 = 0; f_10c = 0; f_110 = 0xffffffff. Two unrelated subsystems use the same template: callers 0x5f8e48 and 0x67bfd0.

name: maybe_Os_SignalAndClose
summary: If the runtime object exists, wakes its waiting thread and then sends the close/notify request; part of the service-call bracketing used by the session wrappers 0x10cde0 / 0x10d430.
evidence: iVar1 = 0x11f20c(); if (iVar1 != 0) { 0x11f730(iVar1); 0x11973c(); }. 0x11973c is the svc-0x32 stub with header 0x190000. Callers 0x10cde0, 0x10d430, 0x51c38c.

name: maybe_Os_IsSessionRunnable
summary: Returns 1 only when the session is open and both the connected (0x20000000) and ready (0x10000000) bits of its status word are set.
evidence: uVar1 = 0x113954() status word, iVar2 = 0x1139b0() open flag, result = (open && (status & 0x20000000) && (status & 0x10000000)). Its only caller 0x10d430 uses the result to decide whether to arm the in-call flag.

name: maybe_StaticInit_ThreeWordArray
summary: Constructs a three-element, 4-byte-stride temporary array through the shared array-ctor helper; Ghidra lost the rest of the body, so only the construction is visible.
evidence: Only statement: func_00100050(local_1c[12], g_00114270, 4, 3), and the caller-less function is marked noreturn. Same 'stack array of static objects' idiom as 0x1143f4.

summary: Constructs a two-element array of 0x10-byte records on the stack through the shared array-ctor helper; everything after the construction was truncated by Ghidra.
evidence: func_00100050(local_30[36], g_001144b0, 0x10, 2). Called from 0x10cde0 and 0x10d430 immediately before they send their request, so this is the local request-structure setup Ghidra could not follow.

name: maybe_Svc_SendRequest3
signature: int maybe_Svc_SendRequest3(u32 handle, int cmd, u32 arg3)
summary: Builds a five-word IPC request in the calling thread's command block (header, command, argument, handle, command<<14|2) and issues svc 0x32 (SendSyncRequest), then returns the reply word.
evidence: coproc 10,6,7 yields the thread command block; f_80 = g_0011450c (header), f_84 = arg2, f_8c = arg3, f_94 = arg1, f_90 = arg2<<0xe|2; software_interrupt(0x32) = SendSyncRequest; returns iVar3->f_84 when the result is >= 0. Only caller 0x10cde0.

name: maybe_Svc_QuerySessionInfo
signature: int maybe_Svc_QuerySessionInfo(u8 cmd, u8 *out0, u32 *out1, u32 *out2, u32 *out3)
summary: Sends a one-byte command to the session and copies the four reply words back to the caller; used to poll the session state before a request is made.

name: maybe_Svc_SendRequest4

summary: Six-word IPC request builder used by the retrying wrapper 0x10d430: packs arg3<<14|2 as the request descriptor, issues svc 0x32 and returns the reply.

name: maybe_Svc_PollStatusFlags
summary: Refreshes a pair of one-byte status flags from the service and, when the returned mode word changes to the expected value, switches the runtime to the new mode.

name: maybe_Fs_ArcHeader_Parse
summary: Parses a three-section archive header: checks the magic word and a size field (0x1000000..0x1000100), then resolves the three sub-blob offsets and returns pointers to each payload (each +8 past its header word).
evidence: if (*arg2 == g_00114e5c && arg2[2] - 0x1000000 < 0x10001) then 0x11bb70 / 0x11bb08 / 0x11bbdc locate the three sections and the results are stored as +8 offsets; out array is three pointers. Callers 0x10e08c and 0x54a3b8.

name: maybe_Os_WorkQueue_Push
signature: u32 maybe_Os_WorkQueue_Push(WorkQueue *q, int wait, u32 arg3, int *node)
summary: Publishes the next work item: waits until a free node is available, drains the completion queue (folding finished item ids into f_188/f_18c), links the new node at the tail and returns the item's sequence number.
evidence: Uses 0x11b8c0(q,4) to reserve a node, 0x11c8e0(&q->f_b4,&local) to pop completions while none is free (sleeping via 0x11cc94), maintains q->f_16c/f_170/f_174 (tail pointer, last id), and 0x11c96c / 0x1166b4 to hand the node over. Callers 0x10e104, 0x10e174, 0x543484, 0x546220, 0x547934, 0x5517d0, 0x5518f4.

name: maybe_Os_WorkQueue_Drain
signature: void maybe_Os_WorkQueue_Drain(WorkQueue *q, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, int *node)
summary: Discards every pending completion of a work queue: pops each finished node, records its item id and clears the matching in-flight id when it was the last one submitted.

name: std_memcpy
summary: memcpy: copies bytes with an unrolled 32/16/8/4/2/1-byte ladder, loading eight words at a time while more than 0x20 bytes remain; returns the end of the destination in the second return register.
evidence: Body: while (bytes > 0x1f) copy 8 words (ldm/stm via HintPreloadData hints), then a bit-test ladder for 0x10 / 8 / 4 / 2 / 1; 385 callers, all record/struct copies (e.g. 0x10f448 copying 0x168-byte blocks, 0x1926d4 copying a 0x84-byte text-style record).

name: maybe_Pack_HandleApplyIfLoaded
signature: void maybe_Pack_HandleApplyIfLoaded(u32 arg1, u8 index, int *handle, u32 value)
summary: If the caller holds a live handle, looks the indexed pack record up and - unless the record is still in state 1 - applies a value to the handle's object.
evidence: if (*arg3 != 0) { puVar1 = 0x11cb38(&tmp); iVar2 = 0x11bac0(*puVar1, arg2); if (iVar2 == 0 || *(char*)(iVar2+4) != 1) { 0x11b530(*arg3, arg4); } } - the same record-type test used by 0x116e44 and 0x11ae88.

name: maybe_Pack_ApplyToLoadedHandles
summary: Pushes a value into every live handle of a streamed slot (the two buffers at +0x34/+0x3c, the pack-backed one at +0x40 and the 5 x 32-record table at +0x7c) provided the corresponding pack record reports type 2.

Callers 0x105584, 0x105ace, 0x105afc, 0x1eb8c8.

name: maybe_Os_InvokeCallbacks
summary: When a pending-event bit is set, invokes up to eight registered callback slots, then (if a callback asked for it) waits for the runtime object to drain and closes it.
evidence: *g_001188a8 is a state block: byte +1 = pending mask, +2 = handled mask, +8 = handle. Loop i < 8 calling table[*g_001188ac + i*4]; then while (0x1180b0(g_001188b0) == 0) sleep 0x11cc94; 0x1186b8(handle); 0x118064(). Callers 0x10cde0, 0x10d430, 0x119af4, 0x51c254.

name: maybe_Svc_SendRequest190000
summary: One-word IPC request with the fixed header 0x190000 and a single reply word; part of the service bracketing used by the session wrappers.
evidence: Thread command block f_80 = 0x190000, svc 0x32, on success result = f_84 and *reply is left in f_84's neighbour; only caller 0x113814 (signal-and-close).

name: Snd_Channel_Release
summary: Releases one channel object: unlinks and frees its parameter list, recomputes the volume/pan of each remaining sub-voice, and returns all recycled list nodes to the pool.
evidence: Walks self->f_28 (removing entries of type 2 via 0x11fcf8) and the list at +4 (calling maybe_Snd_CalcVolumePan@0x11b048 on each 0x108-byte owner), then recycles from a 0xc-byte, 0x80-entry bucket table at g_0011b030 after applying UnsignedSaturate(prio,7); only caller 0x10e174 (release all channels).

name: Snd_ChannelList_ReinsertByPriority
summary: Moves a channel between the mixer's priority buckets: unlinks it from the channel list and re-links it under the bucket index derived from its volume+pan priority byte, saturated to the eight priority levels.
evidence: Disassembly 0x11af14: removes the node from the list at +0xc with 0x11ad60, computes prio = usat((u8)node->0x9d + node->0x50, 7) and index = prio*3 into the 0xc-byte, 0x80-entry bucket table at g_0011b030, then inserts with 0x11fcf8(list, node). Companion of maybe_Snd_InsertChannelByPriority@0x11fd1c (N_032) and of the bucket walk inside 0x11ae88; no direct callers (reached through the channel vtable).

name: maybe_Snd_QueueObjectCommand
summary: Queues a type-9 sound command carrying a value taken from the target object's vtable slot +0x20 plus a caller-supplied subtype byte, and returns the command's sequence number.
evidence: engine = 0x11b7e8(); node = 0x11b57c(engine,6); node[3] = engine->f_184; *(u8*)(node+1) = 9; value = (**(code**)(*obj + 0x20))(obj); node[4] = value; *(u8*)(node+5) = subtype; links at engine->f_16c/f_170 and returns engine->f_174. Callers 0x54455c, 0x545520, 0x546d3a (all in the 0x54xxxx stream player).

name: maybe_Game_GetDataManager
summary: Lazily creates and returns the global game-data context (master tables: monsters, items, text, maps) that the 0x63xxxx lookup helpers take as their first argument.
evidence: One-shot flag g_0011cbc0, cache g_0011cbc4, size g_0011cbc8 via 0x11fe8c + 0x11cfac alignment, std_bzero then vtable store *puVar3 = g_0011cbd0. 992 callers, all of which immediately pass the result to data lookups such as 0x63fd24 (battle slot id -> monster record, test of record->f_191), 0x63cc1c and 0x63d85c.

name: Os_VirtualToPhysical
summary: Translates a virtual address to its FCRAM physical address: VRAM (0x1f000000..0x1f5fffff, plus the 0x1f600000 alias) maps to 0x08000000-based memory, the linear heap shifts by 0x0c000000 or 0x0f000000 depending on the heap base, and unmapped addresses return 0.
evidence: Body: result = 0x123e18(address,1); if 0 and (address + 0xe1000000 < 0x600000 || address == 0x1f600000) -> address + 0xf9000000 (0x1f000000 -> 0x08000000, the classic VRAM mapping); otherwise tries 0x123db4 / 0x123dcc and the heap bounds from 0x122cd8 / 0x122cc0, adding 0xc000000 (or 0xf0000000 for heaps at 0x30000000+). 31 callers, all low-level audio/DSP buffer setup.

name: Os_TranslateLinearAddress
summary: Translates an address that lies inside the linear heap: validates the range against 0x124cdc/0x124cec and returns the physical address by adding the heap's base delta.
evidence: uVar1 = 0x124cec(); if (address >= uVar1 && address + size > address && address + size <= 0x124cdc() + uVar1) return *g_00123e14 + address; else 0. Only caller 0x12345c.

Part of the Squirrel standard library block (0x14cc14 has the 'compare func failed' string).

name: Script_ArrayClone
summary: Copies all elements of one script array into another (the native behind array copy/assign): grows the destination's capacity, copies each 8-byte value with reference-count handling, and releases the elements beyond the new length.

name: maybe_Script_CallFunction2
summary: Calls a script closure with two arguments and, if the VM exposes a result hook, hands the returned value back to it.

name: Event_EvaluateConditionBlock

summary: Evaluates a serialised condition/requirement block (the kind selector plus up to four id lists) against the current game flags: it returns 1 as soon as one listed requirement mismatches the flag bytes and 0 when the whole list matches. The caller ORs the result into a per-entry byte, i.e. it is a boolean predicate over a requirement list.
evidence: The block is an array of 0x28-byte rows selected by row+0x20 == kind; each row has counts and self-relative offsets to lists of (u16 id, u8 mode) pairs that are compared with the flag bytes at gameWork+0x24a98+id (the same +0x24a98 flag area used by 0x15a690); ids are resolved through 0x66b17c (item), 0x66af08 (spirit) and 0x66b380 (quest). Callers 0x1ab690 and 0x1b2448 (menu/quest UI).

name: maybe_Script_CallAllArgs
